subject: Tenant-scope retention and regional-storage offering — ops & engineering alignment
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com, sales-eu@cloudpartner.com
Date: 2028-07-22T09:03:00Z
Subject: Tenant-scope retention and regional-storage offering — ops & engineering alignment

Team —

Acme Health (cc'd) has pushed back on our current 'single global retention' approach in the renewal conversation. They need two things we don't fully support today: 1) per-tenant selectable retention windows (e.g., 1yr/3yr/7yr) with an administrative override for legal holds, and 2) the ability to pin a tenant's stored data to an EU-only region with proof-of-deletion artifacts when data is purged.

Requesting engineering + product to propose a minimal viable offering we can commit to in the next quarter. Key questions we need answered for sales/procurement:
- What is the minimal data model change to tag tenant objects with region and retention-policy?
- Can we produce a reliable proof-of-deletion (hash + timestamp + storage-node id) when a purge completes?
- Impact on storage accounting / billing for tenants moving from global -> regional zones?
- How do legal holds/ediscovery interact with per-tenant retention (override semantics)?
- Rough technical timeline and blockers for: admin UI (select retention + region), admin API, migration script for existing tenants, and deletion playbook for ops.

I've attached a draft retention matrix and a short proposal from Acme (attachments). Hannah — please flag any security/compliance must-haves; Rishi — please note operational backups/archive concerns. Karthik/Marissa — could you propose an MVI plan and cost/effort estimate by EOD Friday?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: retention-matrix-draft.xlsx (spreadsheet), tenant-scope-proposal.pdf (pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-22T13:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Tenant-scope retention and regional-storage offering — ops & engineering alignment

Neha —

Thanks for the clear ask and the matrix. Quick technical readout after a fast pass with infra:

Summary: feasible as an MVI, but there are storage and metadata migration implications. High-level design options below (MVI recommendation bolded):

1) Metadata-only approach (MVI): add a tenant-level metadata record (retention_policy, region_pin, legal_hold_id). Tag every object with a tenant_id lookup; purge job consults retention_policy + legal_hold. No immediate data re-sharding required for read paths. Pros: fast to implement (~6-8w). Con: cross-region residency is logical only; for EU-only we still need a migration step to move actual blobs to EU nodes if they exist elsewhere.

2) Region-physical approach: move blobs to region-specific storage pools and enforce write/read routing by region. Pros: strict residency. Con: expensive migration, replication logic, longer (~12-16w).

3) Hybrid: metadata tagging + controlled background relocation for tenants that opt-in to region_pin. Purge proof-of-deletion: we can emit a signed artifact containing object ids removed, deletion timestamps and storage node IDs, signed with KMS. That satisfies most audits.

Edge cases and blockers:
- Legal hold: we need a flag to block purge jobs at object level; eDiscovery queries must query both active store and cold archives.
- Backups/snapshots: our backup retention may retain data beyond tenant purge unless we add deletion markers and run a rekey/removal pipeline. This is the trickiest operationally.
- Accounting: billing must count data in its current residing pool; moving a tenant will trigger a storage re-accounting job.

Suggested MVI implementation plan (sequence with estimated engineering effort):
A. Data model + admin API + docs (2 weeks dev + 1 week QA)
B. Admin UI to select retention & region pin (2 weeks dev)
C. Purge job changes: consult metadata + legal_hold check; produce proof-of-deletion artifact (3 weeks)
D. Migration tooling (opt-in background mover) (3-4 weeks)
E. Ops runbook + testing with a small set of customers (1-2 weeks)

Total: ~8-12 weeks to get a workable MVI (items A–C + ops playbook). Items D+E for full region-enforcement are additional.

I'll open INF-2487 and break down the tickets; see link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2487.

Karthik
Sr. Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: Tenant-scope retention and regional-storage offering — ops & engineering alignment

Thanks Karthik — that MVI sequence looks sensible. Adding product context / acceptance criteria so engineering can size more precisely: 

Product objectives for MVI:
- Admins can set per-tenant retention: discrete choices (1y, 3y, 7y) in the Console and via Admin API.
- Admins can request "region pin" which marks the tenant as EU-only; the UI should show migration status and provide estimated time-to-complete.
- Completed purge must produce a downloadable proof-of-deletion archive (signed artifact) visible in tenant audit logs.
- Legal hold must be visible in Console and prevent purge until released; holds should be linkable to external ticket ids (for legal workflows).
- Billing: Console should surface projected storage delta for migration (estimate based on current object counts).

Prioritization ask: Sales needs a committable offering for renewals. Proposed rollout plan:
Phase 0 (alpha): Console + API + proof-of-deletion artifact for Hosted customers with small datasets (handful of tenants).
Phase 1 (beta): Add background migration tooling and opt-in region physical enforcement for Dedicated customers.
Phase 2 (GA): Auto-migration orchestration and pricing calibration for Hosted.

Questions for the team:
- Do we need to treat attachments/blobs differently from ephemeral inference caches? My expectation: caches TTL remain separate; retention applies to canonical customer data (prompts, records, embeddings).
- Who will own end-to-end acceptance tests (product or security)? I suggest product + security pairing for test cases around proof-of-deletion.

I'll block time on Friday for a 30m sync if we have a technical plan ready.

—Marissa
Product Lead, Compliance & Governance

Subject: Re: Tenant-scope retention and regional-storage offering — ops & engineering alignment

Quick ops note:

- Backups & snapshots: our current backup system takes periodic snapshots that live in a separate long-term store. For a tenant purge to be auditable, we need a deletion-marking mechanism that triggers an expunge pipeline that can remove objects from snapshots or at least mark them as logically deleted and redact indexes. Full physical deletion from immutable backups may require a snapshot re-ingestion process — costly and slow.

- Proof-of-deletion artifact: agreed we can sign a manifest. We should also emit a purge run id that ops can reference with job logs + node-level checksums. Expectation: purge completion for mid-sized tenants (~500GB) could be several hours to a few days depending on migration throttles. We need a documented SLA we can promise to customers.

- KMS/HSM implications: deletion artifacts should be signed with a tenant-scoped KMS key to avoid cross-tenant verification ambiguity. If a tenant opts for private KMS, we need a fallback for signing artifacts.

I'll work with infra on a runbook for purge failures and a 'safe-rollback' for accidental deletes. Ops wants the admin API to include a dry-run mode and a required two-step confirmation for destructive operations.

Rishi
Head of Infrastructure Operations

Neha/Marissa/Karthik —

Thanks for pulling this together. From Acme Health's side: our contract requires EU-only storage and a 7-year retention for patient-adjacent data, with legal hold overrides tied to litigation IDs. Two asks to confirm for procurement:

1) Proof-of-deletion must include a signed manifest (object ids + timestamps + node ids) and an audit trail showing the legal hold release event. Can you confirm the artifact will be downloadable as a tamper-evident file?

2) Purge SLA: we need a guaranteed maximum time-to-purge once retention expires or legal hold is released (Acme requests <= 14 days for full purge and proof artifact). We understand migration from global to EU may take longer up-front; please provide a migration ETA per tenant size band.

If you can provide a clear MVI commitment and a migration ETA table, procurement can move the renewal forward. Happy to join a sync with engineering next week.

Regards,
Jane Park
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Health
